title: Avars
fact_summary: A steppe people who ruled an empire in the Carpathian Basin from 568 for about 250 years. Genome studies trace their elite to the Mongolian steppe.

claims.text: A 2019 study says that “From 568 AD the Avars established an empire in the region lasting nearly for 250 years”.
claims.certainty_reason: One study's summary of the written record.

claims.text: It reports that most Avar-age men it sampled carry eastern Eurasian paternal lineages “typical for modern north-eastern Siberian and Buryat populations”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: A separate team produced genome data from 66 pre-Avar and Avar-period individuals, including the 8 richest Avar-period burials, and reports that these individuals “carried Northeast Asian ancestry matching the profile of preceding Mongolian Steppe populations”.
The arrival of the Avars in Europe in the 6th century “broadly correlates with the collapse of the Rouran Empire” in Mongolia.

held_by.who: Maróti et al. (2022), following earlier historians

claims.certainty_reason: A match in timing, not proof of a link.

claims.text: The Avar elite reached the Carpathian Basin by a rapid, long-distance migration from the Mongolian steppe.
claims.certainty_reason: Argued by one team, from the abstract; the full article has not been read.

open_questions.text: Was the Avar elite a small ruling group over a mostly local population, as the genome studies suggest?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
